answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted attestation: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before joining, and peers can slash it when they catch duplicate identities. Think of the tundra, a vast sparse plain where every camp is visible from far away: the network keeps a public map of deposits, so spinning up many fake agents costs real money each time. Violet tags mark verified stakes in the registry, while saffron flags highlight suspicious clusters of identical behaviour, letting honest peers route around them instead of trusting every new face.
